elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: New Ownership section: "The Company owns all deliverables and work product created for the Company under this Agreement, including the Site, the Content and the design and look and feel of the Site".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: "HDI hereby assigns all such deliverables and work product to the Company" — present-tense operative assignment from Vendor to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any HDI intellectual property embedded in such deliverables".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: "The Company retains all rights in the Content and in all customer, order, user and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company" — covers every category of Customer data, not just named types.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "any license of such data to HDI is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services"; no retained HDI right to resell, distribute or independently exploit Company data appears elsewhere in the cited text.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "No intellectual property shall be jointly owned by the Parties."

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: "HDI retains its pre-existing intellectual property" preserves Vendor ownership of its own tools/know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The inserted licence runs only to "HDI intellectual property embedded in such deliverables"; the Deliverables themselves are assigned to the Company rather than licensed, so no perpetual deliverables licence is granted (unnecessary at the preferred level).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence exists in the insertion — only ownership/assignment plus an embedded-IP licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No "worldwide" qualifier appears anywhere; the embedded-IP licence is perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free only.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No deliverables licence granted; royalty-free applies only to embedded HDI IP.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No express use/modify licence language for Deliverables (ownership makes it unnecessary at the preferred level).

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "any license of such data to HDI is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services".

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: the cited text contains only artistic/editorial control (5.2) and a Company-to-HDI trademark licence (6.1); nothing allocates ownership of the Site, work product or Company data.

All nine preferred elements are met in operative language in a single inserted Ownership section — Customer ownership, express present assignment, Vendor retention of pre-existing IP, a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence back, Customer retention of all rights in its Content and data, a solely-to-provide-the-Services limit on HDI's data licence, and an express no-joint-ownership sentence. The preferred level is position-complete.
The fallback level is incomplete (no perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free use-modify-sublicense licence to Deliverables), but that is irrelevant because the preferred checklist is fully met.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion into a silent agreement, no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, and no duplication of existing operative terms. The "including the Site, the Content and the design and look and feel of the Site" wording functions as necessary scope anchoring against Section 5.2 (which grants only editorial control) rather than as a gratuitous illustration.

Intent is preserved: Section 5.2 acceptance/approval mechanics, the General Manager provisions and the Deerskin trademark licence in 6.1 all survive without contradiction; Company ownership of the Site is consistent with HDI's hosting and development role.

Repair note (non-blocking): confirm "the Services" is a defined or clearly used term in this Site Development and Hosting Agreement; if it is not, change to "solely to provide the development and hosting services under this Agreement" to avoid an undefined term.
Repair note (non-blocking): the inserted section is rendered as an unnumbered "Ownership." heading — give it the Section 5.5 number referenced in the comment so cross-referencing remains clean.
